title: World container
description: How big the grid is inside a thing that stands in the district holding a loot table -- a cupboard, a car boot, a supply locker. The kind is free text everywhere else (a district's `containers` list, a map site's `container` key, SimContainers.hud_clause's prose), so this file is the one place a kind acquires a shape. A kind with no entry here opens at SimContainers.DEFAULT_GRID rather than refusing, which is what keeps a district free to name a new one. Validated by npm run godot:validate only: the frozen TypeScript oracle's CONTENT_TYPES does not list this directory, so its Ajv never sees it and the nested `grid` block is judged by godot:check:loot's CONTAINER lane instead.

id.description: Stable namespaced id, always container.<slug>. Permanent once shipped.

kind.description: The word a district or a map site uses for this thing, and the word SimContainers.hud_clause puts in the player's sentence. Matched exactly; two entries naming one kind is a content error godot:check:loot refuses.

grid.description: Cells across and down, on the same scale as a pack's: one cell is about a fist (docs/10). A cupboard holds more than a car boot because a cupboard is bigger, not because it is worth more -- what it *yields* is the loot table's business and nothing here.
